root_idea.summary: The root centers on releasing or leaving something unrestrained, and also has a distinct branch of earnest supplication or mutual imprecation; a third lexical branch concerns scant water.
root_idea.development: The release sense appears in leaving a person or animal to itself, with related uses for being unprovided or at liberty. The supplication sense develops into earnest, humble prayer and into mutual invocation of a curse; the sources also record a separate sense of paucity of water.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form VIII verb with independently supported lexical interpretations in the supplied Quranic evidence.

senses.definition: To join in invoking God's curse upon whichever party is lying or in the wrong.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic first-person plural construction at 3:61, the verb denotes mutual imprecation; the related noun مُبَاهَلَةٌ names this act of invoking the curse on the wrongdoer.

senses.definition: To humble oneself and address God with earnest, sincere supplication.
senses.usage_conditions: In the same Quranic construction, the verb is also explicitly explained as striving earnestly and humbly in prayer; this interpretation accounts for renderings such as “let us pray humbly.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave a she-camel without an udder-band, allowing her to be milked or allowing her young to suck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A related intransitive use describes the camel whose udder-band has been loosened and whose young has been left free to suck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave a person to his own will, opinion, or judgment; to leave him to himself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is used for abandoning a person to act without direction or restraint.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave someone to his own will or disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This Form IV causative use is explained by comparison with an animal left unrestrained.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To curse; a curse or invocation that God curse someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun بَهْلَةٌ is used in expressions such as “the curse of God be upon him.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Scant water or paucity of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a separate lexical branch from release and supplication.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sending or letting flow of water over a sown field after sowing has been completed.
To milk a camel after removing its udder-band; of a young camel, to pull off the band and suck its mother.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry records both the milker's action and the young camel's removal of the bands.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave subjects or a community unrestrained, free to do as they please.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: By extension, a place such as the shores or desert may be said to leave people free in their settlements, beyond the reach of authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The quality of shrinking from foul things together with generosity or nobility.
A person who avoids foul things and is generous or noble; also, a lord, chief, or prince combining good qualities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is applied to both men and women in the cited lexical record.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great or frequent laugher.
Of a camel, having no udder-band, nose-rein, or brand, and thus being left free.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can describe a camel whose udder-band has been loosened and whose young has been left free to suck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom, to come with one's property fully at another's disposal, withholding nothing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This figurative use occurs in a woman's address to her husband and expresses making all her property lawful or available to him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: People living at liberty in their place of abode, beyond the reach of a ruler and free to do as they please.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative plural use of the adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Going to and fro without work.
A shepherd without a staff, or one walking without a staff.
A man without a weapon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use describing lack of customary equipment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman without a husband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use synonymous with being unmarried or without a spouse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fruit of a tree identified in the lexical record with the juniper or a related tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources describe differing botanical identifications and medicinal uses for the fruit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To let oneself loose upon someone or something, acting without restraint and overwhelming or destroying it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This use is preserved from a poetic illustration and is distinct from the Quranic supplication sense.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Leaving a person to his own will represented.

cautions: The sole Quran occurrence is the first-person plural imperfect نَبْتَهِلْ; the public headword is normalized to the Form VIII perfect اِبْتَهَلَ. The Quranic construction has two explicitly attested lexical interpretations, which are kept as separate senses.
